message:
feat(update): settle the updater's order and failure rules before the dangerous half

This is the state machine with nothing attached to it -- no process is killed,
no file is replaced. That is on purpose. What actually needs to be right here
is the ordering and what each failure does, and those questions get very hard
to reproduce on demand once real termination and replacement are wired in. So
they are pinned first, against a seam a test can drive.

Four rules, each with a test that fails if it is broken:

The lock is never waited on. If another updater or the installer holds it,
AcquireLock is the only call that happens -- not even a manifest fetch.
Deferring an update costs a cycle; two processes replacing one directory costs
the installation.

An unreachable server does nothing at all. No manifest means NothingToDo, not
a failure, and certainly not a reason to disturb a product that is working.

Prepare or Quiesce failing backs out without escalating to a forced shutdown.
The product is busy with something worth more than an update, nothing on disk
has been touched, and the verified download is kept so the next attempt starts
from there.

A failed relaunch does not roll back. The files are the new version and they
are consistent; undoing a good install because it did not restart itself is the
worse outcome. It reports UpdatedButNotRelaunched so it is visible instead of
silent.

Past the swap, everything through the health check rolls back, and a rollback
that itself fails gets its own result name -- it is the one outcome where the
install may be inconsistent and a person has to look.

Verify-then-compare is not re-implemented here; load_manifest's types already
enforce it, and a second copy of a rule is a second place for it to rot. The
test asserts that a bad signature means the installed version is never even
read.

Also records what the earlier wrap-to-saturation change was worth beyond
cross-runtime agreement: the old arithmetic could flip a large version into a
small one, which is the worst possible direction for an update decision.
Saturation never inverts.

qwinsta: console active, rdp-tcp listening -- no RDP session. 57 checks here;
139 and 41 in the two earlier suites still pass. Nothing installed, deployed,
or version-bumped, and no production effects implementation exists yet.
